opening.quote: Good afternoon, Tidewell Home, my name is yeah Sanne.
opening.comment: You gave the company name and your name, but the name came out garbled as 'yeah Sanne', so state your name clearly and cleanly next time.

verification.quote: Can I take your full name and your order number or postcode, please?
verification.comment: You asked for the full name and order number before looking up the order, which is exactly what was required.

understanding.quote: So you're askin when the €84.00 will be back on your card?
understanding.comment: You captured the issue correctly and confirmed it with the caller without asking for information they had already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Refunds are paid within 5 working days of this return arriving, so it will be on your card within 5 working days from yesterday.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The 5 working day timeline is correct, but the policy measures from the return arriving at the warehouse, and you did not confirm the item arrived yesterday for certain before stating the window.

process_compliance.quote: Can I put you on hold for a moment while I check the refund is queued?
process_compliance.comment: You asked permission before the hold, but you did not thank Eva clearly on return beyond 'Thank you for waiting', which is acceptable; no other required step applied.

communication.quote: you for calling Tidewell, Eva. Have a lovely afternoon.
communication.comment: The closing was polite, but the caller's thanks were not acknowledged clearly and the sentence was cut off at the start, so polish your delivery.

closing.quote: Is there anything else I can help you with?
closing.comment: You confirmed the refund was queued, asked if there was anything else, and closed politely, which meets the closing standard.
